quotes.text: Switch to [Wero](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wero.md) in the course of 2026 and 2027
Refunds can remain in a pending state for up to 7 days. After 7 days, if no failure signal is received, the refund is considered successful.
the connected account’s name must map to its actual business, not to the platform.
the following categories are prohibited or restricted from using iDEAL | Wero:

old_evidence.text: Rebrand your integration in the first quarter of 2026 to iDEAL | Wero.
iDEAL | Wero payments can be refunded up to 180 days after the original payment.
the connected account’s name must map to its actual business, not to the platform.

findings: The 2026-11-07 overview retains the 2026-05-03 capture's Dutch-customer/EUR, bank-redirect with second-factor authentication and immediate payment outcome notification; iDEAL | Wero recurring is through SEPA Direct Debit, with Connect, Checkout, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Invoicing and Elements listed. It remains no manual capture and no bank dispute. Product listing alone does not specify a particular UI/SDK or prove an account's enablement or successful payment (old raw lines 17-63, 65-117, 145-151; new raw lines 20-66, 68-120, 147-153; source lines 13-23).

The capture repeats a rebrand-in-Q1-2026 and switch-to-Wero-during-2026/2027 migration notice; since the new capture is dated November 2026, Q1 is a historical timetable, not a future deadline newly verified by this snapshot. The source carries that timetable but uses 'currently migrating' without a precise capture qualification (old raw lines 8-15; new raw lines 9-18; source lines 13, 17).

Refunds still have a 180-day submission window and can remain pending for up to seven days before being considered successful absent a failure signal; that outcome condition is narrower than immediate refund completion. Website registration-number display and connected-account actual-business-name matching remain requirements, distinct from payer redirect and payment result (old raw lines 149-159; new raw lines 151-163; source lines 21-23).

The substantive new section lists prohibited or restricted categories on top of Stripe-wide restrictions, including adult content, cannabis except CBD, NFTs, submerchant payment facilitators, P2P transfers, CFDs, weapons, donation crowdfunding, creator/live-streaming, open-loop gaming, precious metals/minerals and illegal activity. The list is combined 'prohibited or restricted', not an individual classification for each category; it is source policy text captured 2026-11-07, not account-specific compliance verification (new raw lines 165-180; old raw ends line 159; source lines 1-27).

The older and new merchant-location lists contain the same 40 account countries, distinct from Netherlands-only customer location. The older overview's MP4 demonstration, save-details guide and product routes remain listed; a different Elements quickstart URL and heading layout do not deprecate them (old raw lines 65-143; new raw lines 68-145; source line 18).

Both captures instruct merchants using Stripe front-end products to enable iDEAL in Stripe Dashboard before Stripe automatically chooses relevant methods to display (old raw lines 124-129; new raw lines 126-131). The mapped source lines 11-23 omit this stable setup prerequisite. Dashboard enablement and display selection are distinct from customer bank redirect, second-factor authorization, immediate payment outcome notification or paid-funds proof; this is not a November change.

Both captures explicitly mark manual capture support No (old raw lines 53-63; new raw lines 56-66). The mapped source lines 13-23 and reciprocal concept wiki/concepts/stripe-ideal.md lines 16-22 omit this stable limitation despite listing supported products. A manual-capture query needs the explicit negative rather than an inference from product support.
substantive_changes: New explicit iDEAL | Wero prohibited-or-restricted business-category list and scope caveat, absent from the complete older 159-line overview (new raw lines 165-180; old raw lines 153-159).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the older 2026-05-03 and newer 2026-11-07 migration notice as capture-dated statements; Q1 2026 rebrand language predates November and does not prove actual migration completion or exact cutoff (old raw lines 8-15; new raw lines 9-18).

Retain stable Dutch customer/EUR bank redirect, SEPA-based recurring, 180-day/seven-day refund outcome, KVK/equivalent website requirement and Connect business-name rule with original provenance (old raw lines 17-63, 149-159; new raw lines 20-66, 151-163).

Retain Dashboard iDEAL enablement for front-end method display and the no-manual-capture limitation as stable May/November facts, not newly introduced behavior (old raw lines 53-63, 124-129; new raw lines 56-66, 126-131).
conflicts: The iDEAL concept's 'fully switch to Wero API' wording is more specific than either overview's 'Switch to Wero' text and its Q1 2026 instruction is framed as migration in progress (wiki/concepts/stripe-ideal.md line 14; old raw lines 8-15; new raw lines 9-18). Qualify the timing and avoid inferring API endpoint replacement from this overview alone.

The source lacks the newly captured prohibited-or-restricted category section, which is important to eligibility and must not be inferred from its otherwise stable summary (source lines 11-27; new raw lines 165-180).
unresolved_questions: The overview does not establish which of its listed categories is individually prohibited versus restricted, whether a particular merchant is eligible, or whether a migration has completed for an account; policy and account state require their own authority (new raw lines 11-18, 165-180).

The linked Wero migration and SEPA subscription/setup guides carry implementation-specific details; their linked titles in this overview do not establish exact client/server APIs, SDK version, mandate creation or later off-session charge outcome (new raw lines 13-18, 44-46, 140-145).

findings: Add canonical URL and 2026-11-07 pinned raw while keeping the 2026-05-03 raw; add a precise locator and qualified summary of the newly listed prohibited-or-restricted categories (source lines 1-27; new raw lines 1-2, 165-180).

Keep the stable payment, SEPA recurrence, refund, website and Connect business-name facts and capture-date the repeated migration schedule (old raw lines 8-63, 149-159; new raw lines 9-66, 151-163; source lines 13-23).

Add Dashboard enablement as the unchanged front-end display prerequisite omitted at source lines 11-23 (old raw lines 124-129; new raw lines 126-131). Distinguish method display from bank redirect/authentication and success.

Add the explicit no-manual-capture limitation omitted at source lines 13-23, despite the listed supported products; the old and new guides both say No (old raw lines 53-63; new raw lines 56-66). Reciprocal concept wiki/concepts/stripe-ideal.md lines 16-22 also omits it.
conflicts: No direct old/new reversal, but the source's current-migration phrasing can make a passed Q1 2026 milestone look future-tense in the November capture (source lines 13, 17; new raw lines 9-18).
source_assessments.reason: The new capture adds consequential eligibility categories. Independently, the existing source omits stable Dashboard enablement for front-end method display and the explicit no-manual-capture limitation; both need a source correction while retaining dated migration framing.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ideal, the complete 2026-11-07 overview still describes iDEAL | Wero for Netherlands customers paying EUR by bank redirect and second-factor authorization, with immediate payment outcome notification, SEPA Direct Debit for recurring use, no bank disputes or manual capture, and 40 merchant-account countries (new raw lines 20-120; old raw lines 17-117). For front-end products, Stripe directs merchants to enable iDEAL in Dashboard so Stripe can automatically choose relevant displayed methods (old raw lines 124-129; new raw lines 126-131); this setup/display step neither authenticates a buyer nor proves payment. Refunds have 180 days to be initiated and can remain pending up to seven days before a no-failure success determination; Dutch sites need KVK registration display, other sites equivalent registration, and Connect must show the connected account's actual business name (new raw lines 147-163). New eligibility text lists prohibited or restricted categories (new raw lines 165-180). source-stripe-ideal.md captures much of the stable core but omits Dashboard enablement and the explicit no-manual-capture limitation at lines 11-23, and it needs the new category section plus a dated migration schedule.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ideal, the substantive addition is a prohibited-or-restricted business-category list that the old overview did not contain (old raw lines 153-159; new raw lines 165-180); it does not assign every category a separate prohibition grade or prove a merchant's eligibility. The older Q1 2026 rebrand and 2026-2027 Wero switch wording remains dated timetable evidence even though repeated in November (old raw lines 8-15; new raw lines 9-18). source-stripe-ideal.md needs the new category locator and capture-qualified migration language, while the concept's 'Wero API' phrase is more specific than this overview. Heading reorganization and a changed Elements quickstart URL are presentational/navigation, not proof of SDK or endpoint replacement. SEPA recurring requires its separate path; redirect or an immediate notification does not prove settlement, an off-session charge, or refund finality.
